# Damage over Time — skill-DoT damage model

- **Status:** 🔶 Partial
- **Skills affected:** Mind Control, Path of Flames
- **Mechanic tags:** dot, damage-pool, tick-rounding, methodology
- **Last verified:** 2026-07-10 by Tyra

## Setup

SS12. Skill level 16, no gear unless stated. Target: the standard Level-85 dummy (30% erosion resistance, 30% elemental resistance, 50% armor) — see [training-dummy](training-dummy.md). Two skills, both `Spell / Channeled / Persistent`, 2s Damage Over Time, cast speed 0.333: **Mind Control** (Erosion, base 222/sec at L16) and **Path of Flames** (Fire, base 299/sec at L16). "Meter" = the in-game damage-recount readout (span average, not the tooltip — see [training-dummy](training-dummy.md) methodology note).

## Raw data points

Model vs meter, twelve parses (model error in parens):

- Mind Control, baseline: 155.4 → 150.5 (+3.3%)
- Mind Control, +18% Skill Effect Duration: 155.4 → 150.0 (+3.6%)
- Mind Control, +9% increased: 169.4 → 180.0 (−5.9%)
- Mind Control, +27% increased: 197.4 → 210.0 (−6.0%)
- Mind Control, Control Spell (+35.5% additional): 210.6 → 210.5 (0.0%)
- Mind Control, Shortened Duration (+27.5% additional): 198.1 → 210.0 (−5.6%)
- Mind Control, Shortened Duration + 18% Skill Effect Duration: 198.1 → 209.0 (−5.2%)
- Path of Flames, baseline: 209.3 → 210.0 (−0.3%)
- Path of Flames, +9% increased: 228.1 → 240.5 (−5.1%)
- Path of Flames, +27% increased DoT: 265.8 → 269.0 (−1.2%)
- Path of Flames, Control Spell, standing still: 283.6 → 301.0 (−5.8%)
- Path of Flames, Control Spell + 18% increased: 334.6 → 330.0 (+1.4%)

Worst-case model error is **−6.0% / +3.6%**.

## Derived / confirmed formula

`dot_dps = base_per_second(level) × (1 + Σ increased) × Π(1 + additional) × resist_only_mult`, where `resist_only_mult` applies ONLY the target's resistance (no armor term — see [dot-armor-exclusion](dot-armor-exclusion.md)). Order of operations confirmed by the Path of Flames "Control Spell + 18% increased" parse: `209.3 × 1.18 × 1.355 = 334.6` matches the meter (330.0) far better than applying the additional term first.

## Notes / caveats / open questions

**Partial — the residual is unexplained.** Ship with a disclaimer of "may be off by up to ~10%" (a widened safety margin for untested magnitudes; the measured worst case here is 6.0%).

The residual is ~0% with no damage mods and with additional-only mods; it is ~+6% (meter above model) whenever *increased* damage is present. It is NOT pulse damage (frame-by-frame video analysis at 60fps shows pulse damage scaling exactly with the mod: 5.0/tick baseline → 5.5/tick at +9%, a ratio of 1.10), NOT cadence (61-frame pulse period, identical with and without the mod, sd 2.28 frames), and NOT a second damage source (no second damage-number stream anywhere on screen).

The residual behaves like a **constant** multiplicative term, not one proportional to the pools: Mind Control's meter/model ratio was 1.0627 at +9% increased and 1.0641 at +27% increased — a 3× change in the mod moved the ratio only 0.1 pt. All parses in this set use small mods (≤35%); whether the ratio stays constant at build-realistic magnitudes (+150–200% increased) is an OPEN verification item, not established.

**Confirmed, do NOT model:** the in-game `DoT DPS` character-sheet readout computes damage as if a second contained **31** server ticks; a second contains 30. Mind Control baseline: per-tick damage 5.0, sheet reads 155 (`5.0 × 31`), real DPS 150 (`5.0 × 30`). Damage numbers land on a ladder of `per_tick × {29,30,31}` (Mind Control baseline: 145 / 150 / 155). **Path of Flames shows no such offset** (7.0/tick, sheet 209, meter 210 — neither is a clean ×29/×31 rung off 210), so the divisor appears skill-specific, not universal. Applying a blanket 30/31 correction factor takes the worst-case model error from 6.0% to **9.1%** on this dataset — it is therefore deliberately NOT modelled.

Cast speed: no effect on DoT DPS (expected — a Persistent DoT isn't delivered per-cast). Duration: no effect on DPS (tested with +18% Skill Effect Duration alone AND stacked on Shortened Duration). The `Extended Duration` support ("Supports Duration Skills") is socketable onto a Persistent skill but grants nothing measurable here.

`Damage`, `Spell Damage`, and `Damage over Time` increased mods all pool into ONE increased pool (confirmed twice, on both skills).

**Open questions:** the ~6% increased-damage residual and its cause; whether the meter/model ratio stays constant at high magnitudes (test: +150–200% increased on Mind Control, check the ratio stays in 0.96–1.07); why Path of Flames shows no 31-tick sheet offset while Mind Control shows it exactly.

**Open question — above-max-level scaling on DoT:** the engine applies a compounding ×1.10-per-level "above max level" multiplier to HIT damage (`_above_max_mult`). It is deliberately NOT applied to `compute_dot`'s DoT damage — a DoT skill pushed past its max level (20) via +Level of Skills currently caps at the level-20 base rate. This is unsourced either way: the Help DB says the multiplier applies to "all hit damage," which could mean DoT is excluded by design (consistent with DoT being its own regime — no crit, no armor, no added flat, all measured) OR could be loose wording. **Never measured** — Tyra tested at skill level 16, never above max. Current behavior = not applied. The ±10% model disclaimer above does NOT cover above-max-level builds — a level-25 DoT would be ~1.6× off if above-max does apply. In-game test: push Mind Control or Path of Flames above level 20 with a +Level source and compare the tick to the level-20 base. A `testing` agent has pinned the current (not-applied) behavior so a future flip is deliberate, not accidental.

**Open question — `fire_dot_dmg_inc` applicability is inferred, not measured:** the DoT increased-pool whitelist includes `fire_dot_dmg_inc` (applied to Fire DoTs, i.e. Path of Flames). This is an INFERENCE, not a measurement — the recorded audit above only isolated the generic `Damage over Time` stat (tested on both Mind Control and Path of Flames), never a Fire-specific "Fire Damage over Time" mod. Including it is low-risk (it's a DoT-only stat by definition — unlike the hit-affecting `erosion_dmg_inc`, which is correctly excluded as UNVERIFIED — so it cannot leak into hit damage), but it has not been independently confirmed to apply to DoT. In-game test: equip a "+X% Fire Damage over Time" source on Path of Flames and confirm the tick scales.

## Implementation (engine model)

IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-10): `backend/engine/offense.py::compute_dot(source, skill, lookup_level, is_spell, extra_additional)` (~L1101) is the DoT damage stage — presence-gated on `skill.dot_forms_by_level`, returns `(rows, dot_dps, dot_dps_vs_target)`. `dot_dps_vs_target = dot_dps × _target_mitigation_dot(source, dtype)` (~L1155), where `_target_mitigation_dot` (~L526) is the resistance-only sibling of `_target_mitigation` this entry originally anticipated — confirmed no armor term, matching [dot-armor-exclusion](dot-armor-exclusion.md). Increased pool is a hand-picked whitelist, NOT `stat_meta.affects`: `dmg_inc + dot_dmg_inc` always, `spell_dmg_inc` for spell skills only, `fire_dot_dmg_inc` for fire DoTs only (~L1149-1153) — this is narrower than the generic hit-pool reader by design, since a DoT must not pick up unrelated hit-only increased stats. Additional pool is the multiplicative product of `dmg_additional` + `dot_dmg_additional` via the parametrized `_additional_product(source, factors, predicate, keyed_tags=...)` helper (generalized from the old hit-only helper so both stages share code byte-identically for hit skills), times the skill's own `extra_additional` (e.g. Mind Control/Path of Flames' per-channeled-stack `IntrinsicAdditional`). `dmg_additional` is confirmed (not merely modeled) to scale DoT damage — the Control Spell isolation described below still holds and is now load-bearing production code, not a forward guess. Wired into `calculate_offense` right after the Spell Ripple stage, before `_finalize_damage_row_pcts`. Skill-side: `backend/engine/skill_resolver.py` adds `DotForm(base_per_second, dtype, duration=0.0)` (~L30) and `ResolvedSkill.dot_forms_by_level: dict[int, list[DotForm]]` (~L146, default empty — every non-DoT skill is byte-identical to before). `_resolve_dot_skill` (~L594) is the shared resolver registering `mind_control` (~L640, base parsed from `progression[*].values.damage`, erosion) and `path_of_flames` (~L649, base parsed from `values.Descript` instead — its `damage` field is empty at every level) — both `hit_forms_by_level={}` (pure DoT host, no hit component at all), `is_spell=True`, `ChanneledSpec(max_stacks=5, behavior="refresh")`, `IntrinsicAdditional(per=0.215, rating_key="max_channeled_stacks_flat", rating_source="stat")` (dormant at base 5 channeled stacks — confirmed no effect until stacks exceed base). Tests: `backend/tests/test_dot.py` (24 tests: `TestAcceptance`, `TestIncreasedPoolHandComputed`, `TestAdditionalPoolHandComputed`, `TestWhitelistBoundaryNegative`, `TestResistanceOnlyMitigation`, `TestNonDotSkillsUnaffected`, `TestDotDamageRowShape`) — reproduces all 12 data points below to stated precision. Per-support-skill golden fixtures auto-captured additively at `backend/tests/fixtures/support_skill_golden/{mind_control,path_of_flames}.json`. NYI, surfaced but not wired (see `.wolf/memory.md`, 2026-07-10 DoT session note): Mind Control's link-count scaling (3 base + 1/channeled stack) and its two link-scaled supports (`mind_control_concentrate_magnificent`, `mind_control_enthrall_noble`) — would need a numeric `mind_control_links` condition, out of scope for this ship (single-link acceptance number only, links don't multiply single-target DPS per the verified model); `befuddle`/`entice` gate on subsystems that don't exist yet. Routing note preserved from the original draft: a support line phrased `"+X% additional damage for the supported skill"` (e.g. Control Spell) is NOT special-cased in `support_mapper.py`'s conditional-line table — it falls through `map_line` → `map_via_parser` (~L278) → `engine/mod_parser.py::_parse_custom_mod_text`, the authoritative gear/support/talent stat resolver, which assigns it to `dmg_additional`.
